summary:
İstanbul stands under the national framework in force across Turkey; country-level law, detention conditions and healthcare are covered in the national assessment. What is specific to the city is the assembly ban and the policing of trans women on its streets.

The Governorship of İstanbul has denied permission for and locally banned Pride parades since 2015 on security and public-order grounds, with the 2016 to 2018 bans stated explicitly; one source dates the ban to 2014. Water cannon were used against marchers on 29 June 2015. The 2014 march drew more than 100,000 participants, the largest LGBT event recorded in Turkey.

Suppression escalated after the ban. In 2021 police blockaded the route and used tear gas, arresting 25 people. On 26 June 2022 riot police dispersed the march at Taksim Square, blockaded streets in the adjacent Cihangir neighbourhood, shut down public transport to the square and detained 373 people, among them the photojournalist Bülent Kılıç; those held were released after a night in custody. The district governor's offices of Kadıköy and Beyoğlu had banned all Pride Week events for seven days. Arrests continued at 113 in 2023 and 11 in 2024, three of them minors, after organisers moved Pride out of Taksim Square into other public spaces and issued false meeting calls to evade police.

Policing extends to trans women going about ordinary business. On 31 July 2025 İstanbul police stopped around 20 trans women in Beyoğlu for identity checks, recorded their names and filmed them; the report describes the operation as profiling.
tangentialFactors:
The scale of the pre-ban marches is the measure of what was lost: the 2014 İstanbul Pride drew more than 100,000 people, the largest LGBT event recorded in Turkey, and the ban has held every year since.

Enforcement has not been confined to İstanbul. Eight people were detained at a Pride march in İzmir on the same June 2022 weekend, which indicates that the İstanbul bans form part of a wider national pattern rather than a local exception.
localsOnly:
Kaos GL's 2025 monitoring records intensified sealing or closing of LGBTI+ residents' homes in İstanbul, a practice that obstructs access to housing.

The parade ban is not a single order. The Governorship has denied permission every year since 2015, and Pride Week events in districts including Kadıköy and Beyoğlu have been banned for seven days at a time, closing off venues and gatherings residents would otherwise attend.
outOfScopeNotes:
Sources disagree on when the İstanbul Pride ban began: one reference source records bans from 2015 with the 2016 to 2018 orders stated explicitly, while a news outlet reports that authorities have banned Pride since 2014. The sources do not establish whether the ban is a standing order or renewed annually.

No İstanbul Pride arrest or detention figures for 2025 appear in the sources; the most recent counts are for 2024.

Whether the roundup of 31 July 2025 produced charges or only recorded names is not stated in the sources.
